name: Vespid Dynamics Acoustic Mapping Drone AMD-2
product_name: Vespid Dynamics Acoustic Mapping Drone AMD-2
description: A small drone equipped with an array of ultrasonic emitters and receivers that maps enclosed spaces using echolocation, creating detailed 3D maps of rooms, corridors, and structures without line-of-sight. The AMD-2 can be launched into a building through a ventilation grate or window and will autonomously navigate the interior using its acoustic mapping to build a complete floorplan, identifying occupants by their acoustic signatures, locating electronic devices by their operational sounds, and mapping structural elements including hidden rooms and passages that may not be visible.
story_hooks: An AMD-2 acoustic map of a building revealed a hidden room that does not appear on any plans — the room is occupied, and the acoustic signatures suggest multiple people have been inside for days.
An AMD-2 was launched into an abandoned structure and its acoustic map revealed that the building is not abandoned — dozens of heartbeat signatures were detected across multiple floors.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Pulse Carbine PC-6 'Heartbeat'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek quadcopter with an insectoid aesthetic, dominated by four articulated ultrasonic emitter/receiver arrays mounted on extended arms. The central chassis is deliberately compact and aerodynamic, resembling a wasp or hornet with swept-back stabilizers. The frame suggests predatory grace rather than utilitarian function.
physical_description.dimensions: 15 cm rotor-to-rotor wingspan; central body approximately 8 cm long, 5 cm wide
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld and pocketable — 250 grams; easily deployable from a wrist launcher or thrown by hand through confined spaces
physical_description.primary_material: Lightweight graphene-composite frame with titanium reinforcement struts; ultrasonic emitter heads in piezoelectric polymer
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with satin-polished titanium accents; deliberately non-reflective to minimize acoustic interference; micro-textured surface reduces vibration artifact
physical_description.color_scheme: Gun-metal gray primary with electric cyan accent lines tracing the ultrasonic transducer arrays; soft amber indicator LEDs nested in the central hub
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimalist design: one tactile power button (recessed, colored amber); three micro-status LEDs (mapping/armed/signal); flush-mounted optical charging port on dorsal surface; no external antenna
distinctive_features: Four asymmetrical emitter pods with radiating fin-like cooling ribs resembling acoustic horns
Pulsing cyan LED array that illuminates during active mapping to visualize echolocation pulses
Exposed piezoelectric crystal teeth along the leading edge of each arm — deliberately visible to emphasize acoustic capability
Gyroscopic stabilizer rings visible within the transparent rotor guards
Hairline fissures etched into the frame in a circuit-board pattern — purely aesthetic but reinforces the 'mapped space' theme
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Vespid Dynamics corporate logo (stylized wasp silhouette) laser-etched on dorsal hull; regulatory compliance stamps in micro-font; model designation 'AMD-2' in white serif type; QUANTA pricing label (Φ8,400 Tier 2 retail) printed on packaging insert
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually seen hovering in surveillance stance, cyan LEDs pulsing in rhythmic echolocation bursts; exterior shows minor scuff marks from deployment through tight spaces; acoustic windows may exhibit residual dust that technicians regularly clean with compressed air
